name: Discovery Energy, LLC (trading as Rehlko)
summary: BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT: Rehlko is the fourth-ranked data-center gen-set OEM and the only one of the four that is privately held and leveraged, which makes capacity — not demand — the whole of its strategy: it claims 14 GW of deployed data-center capacity, took approximately 1.7 GW of hyperscale backup awards in a single 60-day window in April 2026, and is expanding manufacturing by more than 400 percent through the decade while competing against two vendors that earn materially higher margins. BACKGROUND. Formerly Kohler Energy; Platinum Equity acquired a majority stake in a transaction that closed 2024-05-06 with Kohler Co. retaining a minority interest and a board seat, and the business was renamed Rehlko on 2024-09-17 from the six letters of Kohler. The power business traces to 1920 and the company describes itself as the inventor of the first internal-combustion-engine-driven generator. Headquartered in Glendale, Wisconsin, with regional headquarters at Mosel (Americas), Brest (EMEA) and Changzhou; 80 global locations as of the August 2026 boilerplate, revised down from the "more than 100" carried in 2024-25 material, consistent with the sale of Curtis Instruments to Parker Hannifin for about $1B in September 2025. Brands: Kohler Power Systems, Kohler Uninterruptible Power, Clarke Energy, Heila Technologies, Rehlko Engines and the KOHLER consumer standby line. Revenue, EBITDA, backlog and headcount are not disclosed in any first-party source.
ecosystemRole: We assess Rehlko as the widest single-vendor electrical scope in the standby power room after Rolls-Royce Power Systems, and the only gen-set OEM in this corpus that also manufactures a three-phase static UPS: gen-sets from 60 kW to 4 MW, PD-Series paralleling switchgear to 15 kV and 10,000 A, automatic transfer switches to 4,000 A, the APM controller family, eFRAME integrated enclosures, and the Kohler Uninterruptible Power modular UPS range to 500 kVA per system. Clarke Energy adds a gas-engine EPC arm as INNIO Jenbacher's largest authorised distributor across 27 countries, which is how the 1.25 GW INNIO framework reaches data-center customers. Basis: the KD Series brochures and specification guides, the PD-Series paralleling switchgear brochure, the KUP product range and the INNIO framework release. Collection gaps are unusually wide here and are stated rather than filled: no hyperscaler, colocation landlord or neocloud is named as a customer in any source; no revenue, EBITDA or headcount figure exists first-party; and there is no Rehlko-manufactured battery energy storage product at all.

productsAndServices.name: KD Series industrial generator sets — 700 to 4,000 kW (60 Hz)
productsAndServices.description: The mission-critical diesel line and the company's data-center product. Seventeen 60 Hz nodes run KD700 at 700 kW / 875 kVA standby through KD4000 at 4,000 kW / 5,000 kVA, all at 1,800 rpm on Rehlko-branded engines certified to US EPA Tier 2, with the APM603 and APM802 controllers. Displacement spans 18 to 103 litres across I6, V12, V16 and V20 configurations at 135, 148 and 175 mm bore, 1,100 to 5,699 gross horsepower, common-rail injection to 2,200 bar, PMG alternators with Class H / UL1446 insulation and subtransient reactance below 10 percent, and high-ambient cooling standard to 50 degrees C. The EMEA range is quoted to 4,000 kW at 60 Hz and 4,500 kVA at 50 Hz.
highlights: The KD900-E data sheet carries an explicit header line — "Data Center / Mission Critical Rating - Same as the Standby Rating below" — and "One step load acceptance (out of ISO criteria) - 100%" at performance class G3

"Generators sets accept the rated load in one step outside the ISO8528-5 operating limit values", with an excitation system permitting sustained overcurrent above 300 percent of rated current for 10 seconds

The whole range is HVO-approved to EN 15940, and Rehlko states it is "the first power systems manufacturer to have an environmental product declaration for our diesel gen sets" (ISO 14025 Type III, PEP ecopassport)
Every unit is factory-tested for vibration, rain and ingress, thermal balance and full-load acceptance
The KD3250 at 3,250 kW standby is positioned directly against the Caterpillar C175 and the Cummins QSK60 at the hyperscale node

A published start-to-on-load time in seconds could not be found in any first-party document; NFPA 110 Level 1 and UL6200 compliance on the controller implies the ten-second Type 10 requirement without stating a figure
productsAndServices.positioning: Ranked fourth in data-center generators for 2025 by MarketsandMarkets, behind Caterpillar, Cummins and Rolls-Royce. Trade press describes the segment as an "effective oligopoly." S&P Global Ratings' assessment at the time of the buyout is the most candid characterisation available: the business "faces competition from larger players in the market. These competitors typically enjoy higher profit margins and a larger market share."
productsAndServices.soldThrough: 220-plus distributors across 400-plus distributor locations, plus direct global-account management for data centers
productsAndServices.targetSegments: Data centers (hyperscale, colocation, enterprise and edge), healthcare, water treatment, telecom, airports, mining, military and government
productsAndServices.roadmap: The KD62V12A engine has entered production in EMEA to power the KD2000 to KD2800 nodes; the APM804 controller is rolling out across 700 kW and above

productsAndServices.name: KD Series 60 to 600 kW — the completed global range
productsAndServices.description: Launched 2025-12-02, extending the KD family into a unified 60 kW to 4 MW-plus global range. Phase one North American nodes run KD80/KD100/KD130 on a Rehlko 4.5-litre four-cylinder, KD150/KD180/KD200 on a 6.7-litre six, and KD230 through KD300 on an 8.9-litre six, all at 1,800 rpm, all EPA Tier 3, with the APM402 and APM603 controllers.
highlights: Enclosure sound levels published at 70 to 75 dB(A) at 7 m across the range
"Designed to meet ISO8528-5 G3 load acceptance performance" — each model stated to meet class G3, described by the company as the highest standard for load response in the industry

Note the emissions step: the small range is Tier 3 while the entire 700 to 4,000 kW range is Tier 2, because the stationary emergency class is looser than the nonroad classes the smaller engines fall under
productsAndServices.positioning: The edge and enterprise node band, and the range that completes a catalogue a single-source buyer can specify end to end
productsAndServices.targetSegments: Edge data centers, commercial and light industrial standby

productsAndServices.name: KG Series and REZX gas generator sets — 25 to 500 kW
productsAndServices.description: The gaseous range, at 3-phase 480 V: KG25 through KG200 on natural gas and LP, then the 250REZXB at 260 kW natural gas standby through the 500REZXD at 500 kW, with prime ratings published for the 250 to 400 kW nodes. Twenty-three gaseous SKUs are listed against 53 diesel SKUs in the product catalogue.
highlights: Controllers are the APM402 and APM603, the same family as the small diesel range
The gas line stops well below the diesel range's top node — Rehlko's large-node data-center answer is diesel, with gas prime power delivered through Clarke Energy and INNIO rather than in-house
productsAndServices.positioning: A commercial and light-industrial gas range rather than a data-center prime-power product

productsAndServices.name: PD-Series paralleling switchgear
productsAndServices.description: Three tiers. PD-2000 is a low-voltage switchboard to UL/cUL 891 with bus ratings to 10,000 A, short-circuit to 200 kA and a maximum 600 V; PD-3000 is low-voltage switchgear to UL/cUL 1558 with bus to 9,200 A; PD-4000 is UL/cUL-listed medium-voltage metal-clad switchgear to 15 kV with bus to 3,000 A and short-circuit to 150 kA. All three are NEMA 1 and 3R, 50 and 60 Hz, carry a 15-inch colour touchscreen, and parallel up to 32 generators.
highlights: Transition types across the range: open, closed and soft (ramp) transfer
PD-2000 offers rear-access as standard with front-access optional and a shallow 36 to 42 inch depth, plus UL 489 fixed or drawout breakers

Onboard paralleling on the gen-set controller allows up to eight sets of mixed sizes and fuel types to parallel without a master control panel, with load management for up to 16 loads and RS-485 Modbus RTU, Ethernet Modbus TCP, SNMP and BACnet
The switchgear meets UL6200 and NFPA 110 Level 1, with 24-hour rolling data capture
productsAndServices.positioning: Selling the paralleling layer alongside the engines is what makes the single-source pitch real; the medium-voltage PD-4000 in particular is a product most gen-set OEMs do not carry.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Direct and through distributors, engineered to the site's sequence of operation
productsAndServices.targetSegments: Multi-megawatt paralleled standby plants, data centers, healthcare campuses

productsAndServices.name: Kohler Uninterruptible Power (KUP) — three-phase static UPS to 500 kVA per system
productsAndServices.description: The UPS business, trading as Rehlko and migrated from kohler-ups.co.uk to ups.rehlko.co.uk. The range: PW 9500DPA at 100 to 500 kVA from five 100 kVA hot-swappable modules, up to 96 percent true online efficiency and 99 percent or better in eco-mode; PW 9250DPA in a 50 to 300 kW frame scalable to 1.5 MW at 97.4 percent, claimed as the most energy-efficient UPS in its class; PW 8000DPA at 10 to 200 kVA parallelable to 400 kVA in tower or 19-inch rack; PW 6000 at 60 to 500 kVA standalone transformerless with power density to 363 kW per square metre and parallelable to 5 MVA; and PW 5000/TP at 10 to 50 kVA true online double conversion at 95.5 percent.
highlights: The PW 9500DPA claims 99.9999 percent — six nines — availability, with an Xtra VFI mode and, from 2022, island and grid-interaction modes for energy-storage functionality
Battery options span VRLA lead-acid, Samsung lithium-ion and Vision lithium-ion; from August 2024 KUP also offers ZincFive nickel-zinc battery cabinets, announced for the UK and Ireland

A KUP-published article describes the PW 9500DPA as suiting data centres "from 100 kW up to 3MW" through paralleling, while the product page caps a single system at 500 kVA — the 3 MW figure is a paralleled-system claim
Also sold: MF Series, MiniPower Plus, PW 1000 and 3000 single-phase units, and EL100XA / EL300 / ELMOD emergency-lighting central battery systems
productsAndServices.positioning: A credible mid-tier European supplier that does not register in any published data-center UPS market-share ranking. Across four independent vendor sets covering data-center UPS — MarketsandMarkets, ResearchAndMarkets, GMInsights and a 2025 restatement — the named leaders are Schneider Electric, Vertiv, Eaton, ABB, Huawei and Delta, with Schneider alone above 24 percent share; Piller appears in these rankings and Kohler does not.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Direct and through channel partners, predominantly in the UK, Ireland and EMEA
productsAndServices.targetSegments: Medium and large data centres, pharmaceutical, commercial fit-out, telecom, healthcare

productsAndServices.name: eFRAME integrated enclosures and Skin-Tight enclosures
productsAndServices.description: eFRAME is the walk-in modular enclosure system for backup generator solutions up to 4 MW, marketed for mission-critical and data-center use and sold factory-direct with high sound attenuation — and it is the product the new Kenosha, Wisconsin plant is being built to assemble. Skin-Tight is the tighter-fitting alternative, UL 2200 factory-certified and IBC seismic-certified, OSHPD pre-approved to 2,500 kW.
highlights: Skin-Tight carries a 186 mph wind rating, Florida Building Code impact rating to 1,750 kW, and a Power Armor finish surpassing 3,000 hours of salt spray to ASTM B117
AQMD options are offered on eFRAME walk-in enclosures — an explicit accommodation for California South Coast air-quality permitting

Enclosure assembly is the capacity bottleneck Rehlko is spending against: Kenosha is a 160,000 sq ft facility with production from late 2026 and full capacity in early 2027, with "a significant portion of the facility's planned capacity already committed"
productsAndServices.positioning: The integration layer that turns a gen-set into a delivered, permitted, sound-attenuated installation — and where Rehlko is competing on repeatable architectures and standardised delivery rather than on the engine
productsAndServices.targetSegments: Hyperscale and colocation data centers, mission-critical

productsAndServices.name: Clarke Energy — gas-engine EPC and INNIO Jenbacher distribution
productsAndServices.description: "The largest authorised distributor and service partner for INNIO Jenbacher gas engines in 27 countries," with more than 550 field service engineers globally. Delivers EPC, feasibility, design engineering, project management, commissioning, long-term service agreements, remote monitoring and spare parts across gas engines, data centres, battery storage, microgrids, hydrogen (electrolysers and hydrogen-fuelled engines), biogas upgrading and carbon recovery. Its data-centre pitch is "resilient, efficient, and sustainable behind the meter power systems for data centers and mission-critical infrastructure."
highlights: Clarke Energy is the delivery vehicle for the 1.25 GW three-year INNIO engine framework agreement announced April 2026

Applications span electricity generation, CHP, trigeneration, quadgeneration, peaking stations, hybrid power, standby, remote power and demand-side management; fuels span biogas, natural gas, coal gas, CNG/LNG, syngas, flare gas, propane, furnace gas and hydrogen
UK statutory accounts show revenue of £432.5m in FY2023, up 20 percent, with pre-tax profit of £34.0m against £13.4m — the only audited financial data available for any part of the group
Leadership turned over inside a year of the carve-out: Peter Holliday and James Clarke ceased to be directors on 2025-04-11, with Kyle Quinn appointed president effective 2025-04-01
productsAndServices.positioning: Gives Rehlko a gas prime-power route into data centers without manufacturing the engines — the structural difference from Caterpillar, Cummins and Rolls-Royce, all of which build their own
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Direct EPC and distribution across 27 countries
productsAndServices.targetSegments: Data centres, industrial CHP, grid support, biogas

productsAndServices.name: Controllers — the APM family and MPAC transfer-switch controls
productsAndServices.description: Six current SKUs: APM402 to 1,000 kW; APM603 at 80 kW and above; APM804, launched 2026-05-19 as the Global Systems Controller for KD Series at 700 kW and above; the legacy Decision-Maker 3500 for REZGT, REOZT4, REOZK4 and REOZJ4 models; and MPAC 1200 and MPAC 1500 for automatic transfer switches to 4,000 A at 115 to 600 V. The APM802 also appears throughout the KD 700 to 4,000 literature.
highlights: The APM804 launch cites advanced paralleling, a scalable architecture and "cybersecurity architecture aligned to evolving regulatory expectations" — the first time Rehlko has led a controller launch on security
The Decision-Maker family, long the brand's control identity, is now largely legacy: only the Decision-Maker 3500 remains in the current catalogue
Automatic transfer switches span 30 A to 4,000 A in standard, bypass-isolation and service-entrance forms, with standard, delayed and closed transitions
productsAndServices.positioning: The layer that makes the single-source scope coherent — engines, switchgear and transfer all speaking one control family
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Bundled with gen-set and switchgear scopes

productsAndServices.name: Service, aftermarket and connected monitoring
productsAndServices.description: Rehlko Power Plus is the cloud-based industrial remote monitoring platform, expanded 2026-08-11 to cover 24/7 remote monitoring, real-time alerts, advanced diagnostics, reporting and fleet-wide asset visibility across generators and automatic transfer switches. Conscious Care is a reduced-runtime and extended-maintenance programme that cuts exercise hours, fuel burn and greenhouse-gas emissions. Performance Care 360 is the trademarked service offering. The Wilmott Group acquisition of August 2025 added WB Power Services and Wiltech Acoustics, 19 UK locations and support at more than 4,000 critical power plants.
highlights: Conscious Care is quietly a permitting product: reducing required exercise and runtime hours is exactly what an air permit's hour cap constrains
Wiltech brings enclosure manufacturing in-house in the UK, the EMEA counterpart to the Kenosha eFRAME plant
The Wilmott integration completed 2026-06-16, roughly ten months after closing
productsAndServices.positioning: The service depth that a #4 must build to compete with Caterpillar's and Cummins' dealer networks, assembled partly by acquisition rather than organically
productsAndServices.targetSegments: The installed base across data centres, healthcare and industry

productsAndServices.name: Heila Technologies, Rehlko Engines and Home Energy
productsAndServices.description: Heila Technologies is a distributed-energy and microgrid control platform — Heila Edge, which connects and optimises solar arrays, batteries and other distributed resources. Rehlko Engines sells diesel, gasoline, hybrid and alternative-fuel engines at 2.5 to 112 kW for off-road and OEM applications under Eric Fontaine. Home Energy sells KOHLER-branded commercial-grade residential standby generators, the consumer brand retained within Rehlko.
highlights: Heila's standalone site now redirects to rehlko.com and it has been dropped from the current "Who we are" business list and from 2026 press-release boilerplate, though Platinum Equity's portfolio page still describes it; its status is not clarified anywhere first-party
Heila is control software, not storage hardware — its only public deployment is a community microgrid in Sandwich, Massachusetts
Rehlko also publishes a 100 kW hydrogen fuel-cell power system and, with Toyota, a 1 MW hydrogen fuel-cell generator system
productsAndServices.positioning: The adjacent estate, one part of which — Heila — appears to be being quietly folded in rather than developed

recentDevelopments.headline: Rehlko joined the Wisconsin Data Center Coalition as an energy-resilience member, stating a track record of 14-plus GW of deployed data-center capacity, more than 90 percent of it custom-engineered
recentDevelopments.read: The 14 GW figure is the company's headline credential and the closest thing to a market-position statement it makes; the coalition membership is a Wisconsin siting play as much as a national one.

recentDevelopments.headline: Rehlko Power Plus connected services expanded — 24/7 remote monitoring, real-time alerts, advanced diagnostics, reporting and fleet-wide asset visibility across generators and automatic transfer switches
recentDevelopments.read: Extending monitoring to the transfer switches as well as the engines is what makes a fleet-level service contract sellable against Caterpillar's and Cummins' dealer networks.

recentDevelopments.headline: Rehlko published a definition of AI-ready power infrastructure and an eBook, with CEO Brian Melka stating that "AI introduces a fundamentally different operating reality... redefining AI readiness as the ability to maintain stability, control and performance under continuous dynamic loads with five nines reliability"
recentDevelopments.read: Reframing the sale around dynamic load behaviour rather than outage duration is the correct technical read, and it is also the argument a vendor without a battery product has to make.

recentDevelopments.headline: A 12 million euro, five-year expansion of the Cholet, France power control and distribution plant — 56 percent more manufacturing space, 30 percent shorter lead times and more than 100 new jobs, complete in November 2026
recentDevelopments.read: The only euro or dollar figure Rehlko has attached to any of its three concurrent capacity projects, and the one aimed at lead time rather than volume.

recentDevelopments.headline: 2026 Powering Impact report published: a 19.6 percent reduction in Scope 1 and 2 greenhouse gases against a 2023 baseline and 81.2 percent of waste diverted from landfill
recentDevelopments.read: The annual sustainability report is the only scheduled first-party publication a private company with no earnings calendar produces, and it carries no financial statements.

recentDevelopments.headline: Rehlko and Liebherr announced a capacity expansion at Colmar, France — a roughly 12,000 square metre extension that, once ramped, more than doubles the site's production capacity
recentDevelopments.read: Colmar builds the co-developed Rehlko G-Drive engine for the KD Series, so this is Rehlko's engine capacity even though the investment is Liebherr's — and it is the reason the KD range's supply chain runs France to the United States.

recentDevelopments.headline: WB Power Services fully integrated into the Rehlko UK and EMEA platform
recentDevelopments.read: Completes the Wilmott acquisition roughly ten months after closing, adding 19 UK locations and enclosure manufacturing through Wiltech Acoustics.

recentDevelopments.headline: A new 160,000 sq ft assembly facility announced at Kenosha, Wisconsin for eFRAME enclosures up to 4 MW, described as a critical piece of a plan to expand capacity by more than 400 percent through the decade; production from late 2026, full capacity early 2027, with a significant portion of planned capacity already committed
recentDevelopments.read: The dollar figure and the job count were both explicitly withheld — a private company disclosing capacity intent without disclosing the capital behind it.

recentDevelopments.headline: APM804 Global Systems Controller launched for KD Series at 700 kW and above, with advanced paralleling, a scalable architecture and cybersecurity architecture aligned to evolving regulatory expectations
recentDevelopments.read: The first Rehlko controller launch led on security rather than on function, and the point at which the Decision-Maker identity is retired in all but one legacy SKU.

recentDevelopments.headline: Approximately 1.7 GW of new backup power awards for hyperscale data-center projects in North America secured over a 60-day period, spanning multiple hyperscale campuses, supporting "some of the world's largest digital platforms"
recentDevelopments.read: No customer, order value, unit count or delivery timeline is disclosed, and the word "another" in the headline implies a prior award that appears nowhere in the press-release archive. Trade press restated the figure as 1.8 GW; the company's own release says 1.7.

recentDevelopments.headline: Multi-year framework agreement with INNIO for approximately 1.25 GW of gas-engine capacity over three years, delivered through Clarke Energy as INNIO's authorised distributor, with a significant proportion intended for hyperscale, colocation and enterprise data-center operators
recentDevelopments.read: Buys Rehlko a gas prime-power position it does not manufacture — and puts it on the same INNIO platform that VoltaGrid used for its own 2.3 GW order, which is a shared dependency rather than an exclusive advantage.

recentDevelopments.headline: Rehlko co-established the Infrastructure Masons "Data Centers As A Good Neighbor" working group with Schneider Electric and other stakeholders
recentDevelopments.read: The only sourced link between Rehlko and any other company covered in this corpus, and it is an industry-body collaboration rather than a commercial relationship.

recentDevelopments.headline: The all-new KD Series at 60 to 600 kW launched globally, completing a unified 60 kW to 4 MW-plus range; phase-one North American nodes run KD80 to KD300 on EPA Tier 3 engines at 70 to 75 dB(A) at 7 m
recentDevelopments.read: Completing the ladder matters commercially more than technically: a single-source buyer can now specify one control family and one service contract from the edge cabinet to the hyperscale hall.

recentDevelopments.headline: Curtis Instruments sold to Parker Hannifin for approximately $1.0 billion in cash, net of cash acquired; Curtis had calendar-2025 sales of about $320M and had been acquired by Kohler in 2022
recentDevelopments.read: At roughly 3.1 times sales this reads as an opportunistic sale into a strong market, plausibly for deleveraging — and it removes a growth-adjacent electrification asset from a group with mid-4x leverage.

recentDevelopments.headline: Acquisition of The Wilmott Group completed — WB Power Services, in critical power since 1983, plus Wiltech Acoustics for enclosures; 19 UK locations supporting more than 4,000 critical power plants; price undisclosed
recentDevelopments.read: Buys EMEA data-center delivery depth and in-house enclosure manufacturing, the same capability Kenosha is being built for in the United States.

recentDevelopments.headline: Agreement announced to sell Curtis Instruments to Parker Hannifin, framed as focusing on core enterprise capabilities
recentDevelopments.read: The stated rationale and the leverage position point the same way.

recentDevelopments.headline: A WARN plant-closing notice filed with the Wisconsin Department of Workforce Development by Discovery Energy, LLC d/b/a Rehlko for the Saukville, Wisconsin facility — permanent closure targeted 2025-12-31 with three layoff waves on 2025-08-08, 2025-09-05 and 2025-12-31, affecting 66 workers
recentDevelopments.read: Rehlko declined to give a reason, stating only that it "does not comment on operating matters" — a closure running concurrently with a 400 percent capacity expansion, which is a footprint reshaping rather than a retrenchment, but one the company chose not to explain.

recentDevelopments.headline: Rehlko and Liebherr expanded their strategic partnership on next-generation KD Series generators, with the KD700 and KD750 using the 18-litre Liebherr KD18L06 diesel; the partnership dates to the KD Series launch in 2016 and the engines have endured 100,000 hours of laboratory and field testing
recentDevelopments.read: The engine dependency is the structural fact about Rehlko that distinguishes it from the other three: Caterpillar, Cummins and Rolls-Royce all build their own prime movers.

recentDevelopments.headline: Peter Holliday and James Clarke ceased to be directors of Clarke Energy Limited, with Matthew Wilson and Sharon Wright appointed the same day; Kyle Quinn had been appointed president effective 2025-04-01, succeeding Jamie Clarke after 25 years
recentDevelopments.read: Founder and long-tenure director exits inside twelve months of the carve-out; Companies House also records Brian Melka ceasing to be a Clarke Energy director on 2025-10-16.

recentDevelopments.headline: Kohler Energy rebranded as Rehlko, the name derived from the six letters of Kohler and said to signal reliability, resolve, reinvention and resilience; the logomark is three arrows
recentDevelopments.read: A rename that keeps the letters and drops the association — necessary because Kohler Co. retains the plumbing and hospitality brand and a minority stake in the energy business.

recentDevelopments.headline: Kohler Uninterruptible Power and ZincFive announced that KUP would offer ZincFive BC Series nickel-zinc UPS battery cabinets for data-center backup on select Kohler UPS including the MF Series, with availability announced for the UK and Ireland
recentDevelopments.read: Nickel-zinc is a genuine differentiator in UPS energy storage, and the geographic limitation is the tell on how regional the KUP business actually is.

recentDevelopments.headline: The Platinum Equity transaction closed: Platinum became majority owner with Kohler Co. remaining as an investment partner and David Kohler taking a seat on the board; financial details were explicitly not disclosed by either party
recentDevelopments.read: S&P Global Ratings assigned a 'B' issuer credit rating with a stable outlook on a transaction that trade press relaying S&P valued at $3.325 billion, with leverage in the mid-4x area, interest coverage in the mid-2x area and an EBITDA margin around 10 percent in 2024.

recentDevelopments.headline: South Africa's Competition Commission approved the acquisition with conditions, recorded in the Government Gazette as Discovery Energy Holdings, L.P. acquiring the energy business of Kohler Co.; in South Africa the target comprised only Clarke Energy South Africa
recentDevelopments.read: The conditions — no retrenchments in South Africa as a direct result of the merger, plus capital-expenditure and supplier-procurement commitments — are the only publicly filed regulatory terms of the deal.

recentDevelopments.headline: Kohler Co. announced it would establish its Energy division as an independent business with Platinum Equity as majority investment partner; Bloomberg had reported advanced talks at more than $3 billion three days earlier
recentDevelopments.read: The carve-out rationale as reported: Kohler Co. wanted to focus on plumbing and hospitality, and the energy business needed independent capital to scale.

strategyRead: (High confidence) We assess that Rehlko's strategy is to convert available capacity into share while the leaders are sold out, and that this is the only lever a fourth-ranked, leveraged private company has. Basis: approximately 1.7 GW of hyperscale backup awards in a single 60-day window in April 2026, against an industry running 50 to 80 week lead times on mid-megawatt sets and OEM backlogs allocated into 2028; three concurrent capacity projects — Kenosha for eFRAME enclosures, Cholet for power control and distribution, and Liebherr's Colmar engine extension — and a stated plan to lift capacity by more than 400 percent through the decade. Speed and availability, not price or technology, are what the company is selling.

(High confidence) We assess that the scope, not the engine, is the differentiation. Basis: Rehlko is the only gen-set OEM in this corpus that also manufactures a three-phase static UPS and medium-voltage metal-clad paralleling switchgear. The PD-4000 reaches 15 kV, the PD-2000 reaches 10,000 A of bus and 200 kA of short-circuit, the transfer switches reach 4,000 A, the APM controller family spans all of it, and the KUP range runs to 500 kVA per system and 5 MVA paralleled. After Cholet the company describes the offer as "a single, fully integrated power infrastructure package." This is a bet that the buyer who wants one throat to choke is a large enough market — which is a different customer from the hyperscaler with an in-house power-engineering team.

(Moderate confidence) We assess that the engine dependency is the structural risk the other three do not carry. Basis: the G-Drive engines for the entire 700 to 4,000 kW range are co-developed with and manufactured by Liebherr at Colmar in France, and the power control and distribution business manufactures at Cholet. Caterpillar, Cummins and Rolls-Royce all build their own prime movers. Two consequences follow: the capacity ceiling on Rehlko's highest-value nodes is set by a partner's investment decision, which is why the Colmar extension is announced jointly; and the supply chain into the American data-center market runs France to the United States, a tariff exposure on which Rehlko publishes nothing at all.

(Moderate confidence) We assess that Kohler Uninterruptible Power is a real business that is not a data-center UPS contender at scale, and that the dossier should say so in both directions. Basis: KUP sells a genuine modular three-phase range with a nickel-zinc battery option, and across four independent market-research vendor sets covering data-center UPS — MarketsandMarkets, ResearchAndMarkets, GMInsights and a 2025 restatement — Kohler and Rehlko appear in none of them, while Schneider Electric alone holds more than 24 percent share and the top five hold roughly 60 percent. Piller, also covered in this corpus, does appear in those rankings. The ZincFive partnership was announced for the UK and Ireland only, which is the clearest signal of how regional the business is.

(Moderate confidence) We assess that the absence of a battery product is a live competitive gap rather than a neutral scope choice. Basis: no Rehlko-manufactured battery energy storage product exists — Heila Technologies is microgrid control software whose standalone site now redirects and which has been dropped from current boilerplate; Clarke Energy integrates third-party batteries as an EPC; and KUP resells ZincFive cells for UPS ride-through. Meanwhile Caterpillar pairs gas gen-sets with grid-forming batteries on named campuses and Cummins took its largest-ever storage order to meet utility-defined requirements for AI load oscillation. Rehlko's own August 2026 framing of AI readiness as maintaining stability "under continuous dynamic loads" describes precisely the problem a battery solves.

(Moderate confidence) We assess that the financial constraint is real and that the disclosure gap around it is deliberate. Basis: no revenue, EBITDA, backlog or headcount figure exists in any first-party source, any year, and the company states plainly that financial details are not disclosed. The only figures available come from trade press relaying S&P Global Ratings at the time of the buyout — a 'B' issuer credit rating with a stable outlook, leverage in the mid-4x area, interest coverage in the mid-2x area and an EBITDA margin around 10 percent in 2024 — which is materially below what Caterpillar and Cummins earn. S&P's own competitive note is that Kohler Energy "faces competition from larger players... These competitors typically enjoy higher profit margins and a larger market share." A further S&P article indexed in January 2026 concerns a proposed term-loan repricing; its contents were not retrievable.

(Low confidence) We assess that the carve-out is still settling operationally, on thin evidence. Basis: a Saukville, Wisconsin plant closed with 66 workers laid off while capacity expanded elsewhere, with the company declining to give a reason; the location count in the boilerplate fell from more than 100 to 80; Clarke Energy's founder-era directors left within a year of the deal; Heila has quietly disappeared from the business list; and one newspaper report notes that UAW Local 833 had raised payroll issues, staffing challenges and contract non-compliance at the Mosel plant. Collection gap: each of these is a single data point, the union account is second-hand through one sentence in one article, and no litigation, customer loss or integration failure was found in any source.

relationships.note: Co-established the Infrastructure Masons "Data Centers As A Good Neighbor" working group with Schneider Electric and other stakeholders.
relationships.context:
Reported 2026-02-11. The working group addresses the community and siting side of data-center development — the ground on which Rehlko also joined the Wisconsin Data Center Coalition in August 2026 as an energy-resilience member.

This is an industry-body collaboration rather than a commercial relationship, and it is the only link between Rehlko and any other company in this corpus that a source explicitly states. No supply, distribution or customer relationship between the two is asserted anywhere.

relationships.via: Shared sponsor and board or advisory ties
relationships.note: Rehlko's board and strategic advisory council carry two senior Vertiv figures, and both companies have been Platinum Equity portfolio companies.
relationships.context:
Rehlko's own strategic advisory council page identifies Rob Johnson as a "Rehlko Board Member" and the former Chief Executive of Vertiv, describing Vertiv as "a Platinum Equity company" and crediting Johnson with leading that 20,000-person business through divestitures, acquisitions and an initial public offering. The same council seats Edward Monser, a current Director of Vertiv Holdings Co. and former President of Emerson Electric.

The link is governance and sponsor lineage, not commerce: no supply, distribution or joint-development relationship between Rehlko and Vertiv is stated in any source found. It is recorded because a private-equity sponsor reusing operating talent across two companies in the same ecosystem is a real structural connection, and because both figures sit where Rehlko's data-center strategy is set.

relationships.note: The market leader, described by trade press as sitting first in what it calls an effective oligopoly in which Rehlko is fourth.
relationships.context: MarketsandMarkets ranks the 2025 data-center generator field Caterpillar, Cummins, Rolls-Royce, Rehlko, Mitsubishi. Rehlko's KD3250 at 3,250 kW standby is positioned directly against the Caterpillar C175. The gap is clearest in prime power: Caterpillar holds named gigawatt-scale gas awards including 2 GW at the Monarch Compute Campus, while Rehlko's gas prime-power route runs through Clarke Energy's INNIO distributorship rather than through engines it manufactures. A trap worth naming: some coverage conflates Rehlko with the Monarch award because one trade article discussed Caterpillar, Cummins and Rehlko together; the Monarch power award is Caterpillar's, with Boyd CAT as dealer.

relationships.note: Ranked second where Rehlko is fourth, and the most direct overlap at the 1,000 to 2,000 kW node band.
relationships.context: Terrapin Consulting Group's 2026 lead-time survey states that "Cummins and Kohler tend to be competitive at the 1,000-2,000 kW range" while placing Caterpillar and mtu at the top of the hyperscale band — the sharpest published statement of where the two actually meet. Both also announced anonymised multi-gigawatt hyperscale commitments within months of each other: Rehlko's approximately 1.7 GW of awards in a 60-day window in April 2026, and Cummins' multi-year framework giving visibility into several gigawatts, disclosed on its Q2 2026 call. Neither names a counterparty. Cummins additionally has a battery product; Rehlko does not.

relationships.note: Ranked third, immediately above Rehlko, and structurally the closest comparison in the set.
relationships.context: MarketsandMarkets places Rolls-Royce third and Rehlko fourth for 2025. The two are alike in ways the American vendors are not: both manufacture their highest-value data-center product in continental Europe and ship it into the American market — Rehlko's G-Drive engines from Liebherr at Colmar and its switchgear from Cholet, Rolls-Royce's Series 4000 from Friedrichshafen with US assembly at Mankato — and both are expanding capacity hard into the same demand, Rehlko by more than 400 percent through the decade and Rolls-Royce by more than doubling Series 4000 gen-set output. Both also sell a UPS alongside the engines, though Rolls-Royce's is a diesel rotary machine and Rehlko's a static one.

policyExposure.regime: US EPA stationary emissions tiers (40 CFR 60)
policyExposure.exposure: The entire KD Series from 700 to 4,000 kW is published as US EPA Tier 2 — the stationary emergency class — and no Tier 4 Final node appears in the current large-node literature. The new 60 to 600 kW range is EPA Tier 3. Diesel catalogue SKUs are listed as US EPA Certified Stationary Emergency. Rehlko's own guide-specification document describes the framework: stationary diesel generators in the US must meet the EPA New Source Performance Standards for stationary compression-ignition engines, with each tier progressively more stringent.
policyExposure.mitigation: The guide-specification template offers "Comply with EPA Tier [2] [3] [4] requirements" as a specifier choice, and the overview brochure cites after-treatment systems, but no Tier 4 Final data-center node is catalogued.

policyExposure.regime: State air-quality tightening above the federal floor
policyExposure.exposure: Rehlko names the risk explicitly in its own guide-specification document: "States, like California, Florida, New York, and Texas, are requiring exhaust emissions conditioning regardless of the [tier]", and "Governing exhaust emissions is becoming increasingly prevalent and is starting to drive generator design specifications." Three of the four states named are top-five US data-center markets, which makes this a direct constraint on the addressable market for a Tier 2-only large-node catalogue.
policyExposure.mitigation: AQMD options are offered on eFRAME walk-in enclosures, an explicit accommodation for California South Coast air-quality permitting; the Conscious Care programme reduces required exercise and runtime hours, which is what a permit's hour cap constrains.

policyExposure.exposure: NFPA 30, 37, 70 (National Electrical Code), 99 and 110 apply across the range; the controller meets UL6200 and NFPA 110 Level 1, and the NFPA 110 Level, Class and Type framework is mapped to NEC Articles 700 and 701 in the company's specification guidance. The KD Series is factory-certified to CSA, NFPA and ISO 8528-5.

A strong compliance position and a genuine differentiator in hurricane and seismic markets: UL 2200 factory-certified, IBC seismic-certified, OSHPD pre-approved to 2,500 kW, a 186 mph wind rating, and Florida Building Code impact rating to 1,750 kW, with a Power Armor finish surpassing 3,000 hours of salt spray to ASTM B117.

Rehlko EMEA material indicates that KD Series models are Stage V certified, but no first-party model-by-model table was retrievable — the EMEA KD Series landing page returned an error during this research pass. The certification claim is therefore carried at the level the source supports and no further.

The full diesel range is HVO-approved per EN 15940, with the company stating this "cuts fuel lifecycle carbon footprint of the fuel by up to 90%", and noting on the KD900-E sheet that HVO volumetric consumption runs up to 4 percent higher. Rehlko states it is "the first power systems manufacturer to have an environmental product declaration for our diesel gen sets" under ISO 14025 Type III and PEP ecopassport.
policyExposure.mitigation: An Environmental Product Declaration is the credential a data-center customer's own carbon disclosure requires, and Rehlko claims priority on it in this product class.

policyExposure.exposure: Collection gap rather than an assessed exposure, and the largest one in this dossier. Rehlko publishes no commentary on tariffs anywhere in its first-party material. The latent exposure is structural: the G-Drive engines for the entire 700 to 4,000 kW range are manufactured by Liebherr at Colmar in France, and the power control and distribution business manufactures at Cholet in France — a France-to-United States import dependency on the company's highest-value data-center nodes. As a private issuer with no filings, Rehlko has no obligation to quantify it and has not.

Recorded as a negative finding. No Buy America, Build America Buy America or domestic-content language appears in any first-party source. The Kenosha, Wisconsin plant, described as building on an existing US manufacturing footprint near the global headquarters, is the closest signal, but domestic content is never claimed — which matters for a company whose large-node engines are French-built and whose customers include federal and government segments.

The South African Competition Commission approved the Platinum Equity acquisition subject to conditions recorded in the Government Gazette: no retrenchments in South Africa as a direct result of the merger, plus capital-expenditure and historically-disadvantaged-person supplier-procurement commitments at Clarke Energy South Africa. In South Africa the target comprised only Clarke Energy South Africa. These are the only publicly filed regulatory terms of the transaction.

periods.commentary: Rehlko is privately held and publishes no financial statements, no earnings calendar and no investor-relations section; the company states plainly that financial details are not disclosed. There is no SEC registrant. The only figures below come from third parties, and the rating-agency numbers reached this dossier through trade press relaying S&P Global Ratings rather than from S&P's own release, which returns an access error to every retrieval method attempted. Aggregator revenue estimates (ZoomInfo at $1.5B, Seamless.AI at more than $1B, PitchBook at 800 employees) contradict each other by an order of magnitude and are not carried.

metrics.name: Consolidated revenue
metrics.result: No credible third party publishes a Rehlko group revenue figure. The defensible statement is that revenue is not disclosed, that S&P indicated an EBITDA margin around 10 percent on a $3.325bn transaction in 2024, and that the group has since divested approximately $320M of revenue with the sale of Curtis Instruments.

metrics.name: Transaction value
metrics.result: Kohler Co., Platinum Equity and Rehlko all declined to disclose terms. The $3.325bn figure is secondary-sourced through trade press quoting S&P and was not verifiable against S&P's own page.

metrics.name: Issuer credit rating
metrics.actual: 'B', stable outlook — Discovery Energy Holdings (S&P Global Ratings)
metrics.result: S&P's competitive rationale, quoted verbatim by the relaying source: Kohler Energy "though boasting diversified revenue streams, faces competition from larger players in the market. These competitors typically enjoy higher profit margins and a larger market share." A Moody's rating exists for Discovery Energy Holding Corporation but its value and outlook are behind a login and could not be read. No Fitch rating was found.

metrics.name: Leverage and coverage
metrics.actual: Debt to EBITDA in the mid-4x area; interest coverage in the mid-2x area (S&P, relayed)
metrics.result: Both figures are as at the 2024 transaction and have not been updated in any retrievable source. A further S&P article concerning a proposed repricing of the term loan was indexed in January 2026; its contents were not retrievable.

metrics.name: EBITDA margin
metrics.result: Materially below what Caterpillar and Cummins earn — Cummins' Power Systems segment ran at 22.7 percent EBITDA in FY2025 — which is the quantitative form of S&P's competitive note.

metrics.name: Debt structure
metrics.actual: A syndicated Kohler Energy Co. LLC USD Term Loan B exists and is broadly held
metrics.result: Confirmed only through mutual-fund N-PORT holdings filed with the SEC, which disclose individual funds' positions. Total facility size, pricing and maturity are not disclosed.

periods.commentary: UK statutory accounts are the only audited financial data available for any part of the group, because Clarke Energy Limited and Rehlko Uninterruptible Power Ltd file at Companies House. FY2024 accounts for both were filed in September and October 2025 but are scanned images without a text layer and could not be parsed in this research pass — they remain the single best untapped source of hard subsidiary financials.

metrics.name: Clarke Energy Limited revenue (FY2023)
metrics.result: Audited UK statutory accounts, reported by Liverpool Business News. Roughly 1,300 employees globally. Director Peter Holliday: "The aftersales part of our business has performed very strongly and we have been able to secure significant new equipment supply contracts."

metrics.name: Clarke Energy Limited pre-tax profit (FY2023)
metrics.result: A 154 percent increase — the gas-engine EPC arm was growing strongly through the carve-out, which is the opposite of the distress the Saukville closure and the director turnover might otherwise suggest.

metrics.name: Clarke Energy Limited revenue (FY2024)
metrics.result: Headline-only: the trade article carrying it is behind a challenge page and the body could not be read, and the currency switch from sterling to dollars is unexplained. Carried at that confidence and no higher.

metrics.name: Curtis Instruments sale proceeds
metrics.actual: Approximately $1.0 billion in cash, net of cash acquired (Parker Hannifin Form 10-Q)
metrics.result: Closed 2025-09-18. Curtis contributed $11m of net sales to Parker from acquisition to 2025-09-30 and had calendar-2025 sales of about $320m — roughly 3.1 times sales.

metrics.name: Disclosed operating scale
metrics.actual: 80 global locations (2026 boilerplate); 220-plus distributors across 400-plus locations and five Power Systems manufacturing sites; Clarke Energy in 27 countries with 550-plus field service engineers; Wilmott adding 19 UK locations and support at 4,000-plus critical power plants
metrics.result: The location count was revised down from the "more than 100" carried in 2024-25 material and still shown on the FAQ page — consistent with the Curtis divestiture. Employee headcount is not disclosed in any first-party source.

metrics.name: Disclosed data-center scale
metrics.actual: 14-plus GW of deployed data-center capacity, more than 90 percent custom-engineered; approximately 1.7 GW of hyperscale backup awards in a 60-day window; approximately 1.25 GW of contracted INNIO engine supply over three years
metrics.result: These gigawatt figures are the company's substitute for financial disclosure. None carries a customer, an order value, a unit count or a delivery timeline, and the 1.7 GW figure was restated as 1.8 GW by one trade outlet — the company's own release says 1.7.
